text.p: Most commodities moved fairly narrowly in offshore markets over the weekend, apart from zinc which rose US$9 a on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on a stocks fall.
Base metals generally held steady levels during thin early London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Friday, though nickel eased following a a sizeable inventory rise of 1,872 tonnes.

Three months delivery nickel was last trading at $7,330, down on its high of $7,360 and Thursday's LME kerb close of $7,380. Traders said the market was finding robust underlying support and was unlikely to show any significant losses following its recent sharp rally of over $1,000. During the early part of 1997, prices have moved from a low of around $6,400 to a four-month peak of $7,490.
Copper absorbed an expected stocks rise of 7,025 tonnes and was last at $2,254, up $6. Traders said copper was expected to consolidate between $2,230 and $2,290 near-term.
Aluminium continued to find good support above $1,600 and managed to absorb a stocks rise.
Traders said aluminium was likely to consolidate on Friday and pegged resistance at $1,625/30.
Zinc after a stocks fall moved to $1,129, up $9, while lead was up $3 at $713 and was also benefiting from an inventory decline. Tin was indicated at $5,990/6,000, versus $5,985.

New York precious metals futures ended slightly higher for the second day in a row Friday, as the complex continued to stabilize following gold's slide to new three-year lows this week on news of a 300 tonne gold sale by the Dutch central bank.
COMEX February gold ended up $1.40 an ounce at $356.40, after trading a $355.00-357.10 range, with total volume estimated at 40,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $355.30/80, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $355.75 and the New York close Thursday at $354.10/60.

A bearish export scene knocked CBOT wheat futures to a lower close as did prospects for increased wheat selling soon due to improved weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said. European grain traders Friday said sales of 1.5 million tonnes of Australian wheat to Iran was done in the low $150.00s per tonne fob, and said Australia was best placed to grab further business with Iran this year because it enjoyed a quality advantage over other exporters.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 6-3/4 at $3.80-1/2.

NYMEX crude ended lower Friday but short covering amid tight supply made losses only modest in the prompt month, and steepened February's backwardation to March when a raft imports are expected to arrive.
The Feb/March backwardation had expanded to more than $1.00 through most of the session. It was 70 cents Thursday.
March crude ended 39 cents off at $24.43 a barrel.
